questions.answer: I'm studying a specific region, so the most important aspects were the language and culture.

questions.answer: The university helped me get my documents in order and helped me get started at the university.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that difficult to find housing. I lived alone but I would recommend living with a host family to get the most out of your stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There aren't any issues with living off campus. Just remember that you need to get your registration which the university will also help you with.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I met with some faculty members and the leader of my department and after talking with me they made a schedule for me that would fit my needs and skill set.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The faculty were quite helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There aren't really any advice. Just talk to the faculty.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The faculty and students were extremely kind but I didn't improve my language skills as much as I would have hoped.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were fine, but maybe weren't the best for exchange students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite different. A lot more memorization and less discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not necessarily unexpected, but the cost of the many different registrations you need - phone, registration of address and extension of visa if you're staying longer than three months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: My rent was a bit expensive compared to the standard, but I was in a bit of a hurry to find a place to stay.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As far as I'm aware there weren't that many activities available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I said, there aren't that many activities available.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend traveling to different parts of the country and experience the beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture because I also had prior knowledge of the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't any parts that I found particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is a very friendly and open society which is very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The professors and the faculty are very nice but a lot of them don't speak english very well, so be prepared for that. 
All my classes were in tajik/Persian. 
You need to be persistent with the faculty/administration to make sure you get the needed documents on time as things moves pretty slow here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a very safe country and I never felt unsafe being alone as a foreign woman.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was experiencing the culture and traveling the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The renewal of the visa and registrations - they aren't the fastest at getting things done, so you need to be on them to make sure it gets done in time so you don't end up paying a fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
